A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the porewater chemistry of the Haiwee sediment was controlled by the extent of reductively mediated Fe mineral dissolution, with the extent of reactivity controlled by the degree of sediment exposure to air.

the gel probe equilibrium sampler provides a novel technique for in situ measurement of As adsorption and desorption in sediments and is a valuable tool for evaluating the effects of porewaters composition on As geochemistry in sediments.

the As sorption capacity in the Haiwee Reservior sediment is controlled by the competition between dissolved phosphate and arsenic for sorption sites, and that this competition is affected by the reductive dissolutions of Fe(III) and the formation of green rust-type phases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gel probe equilibrium sampler can be used to directly assess the effects of pore-water composition on As adsorbability in situ and can provide insight into the factors controlling the distribution of As in sediments.

porewater composition and dissolved As concentrations can have a significant impact on sediment As adsorption, and the effects of these processes can be measured in situ by deploying undoped and HFO-doped polyacrylamides gels in the gel probe equilibrium sampler.

the porewater composition of sediments can control As adsorption behavior, and the gel probe equilibrium sampler provides a unique tool for studying the effects of porewaters on As sorption and transport in the field.
